BiblicalUsage: Morrah is bitterness, trouble of heart — the heart knows its own bitterness, and a stranger does not intermeddle with its joy.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the proverb respects the privacy of sorrow: no one else can fully know what my heart carries, and God knows it all.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
